result.summary: The intersection is a residential environment that lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure, including continuous sidewalks and marked crosswalks. The wide, open roadway design and lack of traffic calming measures create a high-exposure environment for people walking.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: There are no paved walkways for pedestrians, forcing them to walk on the grass or in the roadway shared with vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and left side of the street

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The wide intersection lacks marked crosswalks, providing no designated or protected space for pedestrians to cross.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radii
hazards.description: The large corner radius allows vehicles to make turns at higher speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns and ADA-compliant curb ramps at all crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning traffic.

result.summary: The intersection lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and continuous sidewalks along the main roadway. Large bushes at the corner create significant visual obstructions, and the wide, unmarked roadway increases pedestrian exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Large, dense bushes at the corner of the intersection significantly block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks and curb ramps leaves pedestrians without a designated or accessible path across the wide roadway.

interventions.title: Install Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Provide high-visibility crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps to define pedestrian paths and improve accessibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting and Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove the large bushes at the corner to improve visibility for all road users, a practice known as daylighting.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance, improve sightlines, and slow down turning vehicles.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a complete lack of dedicated infrastructure, such as sidewalks or marked crossings, in a residential setting. Pedestrians are forced to share the roadway with vehicles at an uncontrolled intersection with limited sight lines due to corner fencing and parked cars.

hazards.name: Lack of Sidewalks
hazards.description: Pedestrians must walk in the roadway or on unpaved grass, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the visible roadways.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Intersection
hazards.description: No stop signs or traffic signals are visible to manage vehicle right-of-way at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: The intersection of the two streets in the center.

hazards.name: Sight Line Obstruction
hazards.description: A tall white fence on the corner and parked vehicles on the side street limit visibility for both drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner property with the white fence and cars parked on the right side of the street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to separate pedestrians from traffic.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps at the intersection.

interventions.title: Intersection Control
interventions.description: Install stop signs to clarify right-of-way and reduce vehicle speeds at the intersection.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to improve sight lines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a residential street lacking basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and continuous, well-maintained sidewalks. The wide, unmarked roadway and visible pavement degradation create an environment that prioritizes vehicle flow over pedestrian safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crosswalks
hazards.description: There are no painted markings to indicate where pedestrians should cross the intersection, increasing exposure risk.

hazards.name: Poor pavement condition
hazards.description: A large patch or pothole in the roadway could cause tripping hazards for pedestrians or unpredictable vehicle movements.

hazards.name: Lack of curb ramps
hazards.description: The absence of curb ramps makes the transition from sidewalk to street difficult for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the intersection on the left

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian crossing areas and alert drivers.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at all intersection corners to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Pavement Repair and Maintenance
interventions.description: Resurface the roadway to eliminate potholes and uneven patches that pose hazards to all road users.
